reference_solution.expected_approach: Use binary search on the sorted array by maintaining left and right boundaries and repeatedly eliminating half of the remaining search space.
reference_solution.why: Because the array is sorted, comparing the target with the middle element determines which half of the array can be discarded, reducing the search space by half at each step.
detailed_explanation: Initialize the left boundary to the first index and the right boundary to the last index.
Calculate the middle index between the left and right boundaries.
If the middle element equals the target, return its index.
If the middle element is smaller than the target, discard the left half by moving the left boundary to the position after the middle.
If the middle element is greater than the target, discard the right half by moving the right boundary to the position before the middle.
Continue until the target is found or the search range becomes empty.
pseudocode: Set left = 0 and right = length of array - 1.
While left is less than or equal to right:
If array[mid] equals target, return mid.
If array[mid] is less than target, move left to mid + 1.
Return -1 if the target is not found.
reasoning_steps: Compare the middle element with the target.
Return the middle index if the target is found.
Discard the left half if the middle element is smaller than the target.
Discard the right half if the middle element is greater than the target.
Continue until the target is found or the search range is empty.
edge_cases: Target equal to the middle element

alternative_solutions.name: Linear Search
alternative_solutions.description: Traverse the array from left to right and compare each element with the target until the target is found or the array ends.
